name: Autosomal Dominant Multiple Pterygium Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Dominant Multiple Pterygium Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of multiple web-like skin folds (pterygia) across major joints
Congenital joint contractures affecting elbows, knees, and fingers
Characteristic facial features including micrognathia, cleft palate, and ptosis
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple pterygia and congenital joint contractures with or without characteristic facial dysmorphism, supported by family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical criteria are met

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple web-like skin pterygia across major joints
pathognomonic.notes: Typically involves elbows, knees, and neck
searchTerms: multiple web-like skin folds at joints
webbed skin across elbows and knees

pathognomonic.notes: Fixed flexion deformities commonly affecting large and small joints

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism including micrognathia and cleft palate
pathognomonic.notes: Facial features may vary in severity
searchTerms: distinct facial features with small jaw

common.notes: Lateral curvature of the spine developing in childhood
Reduced muscle tone often present in infancy

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory difficulties due to thoracic cage deformities
occasional.notes: May require supportive care in severe cases
searchTerms: respiratory difficulty due to thorax shape
restricted lung function from chest wall

occasional.notes: Conductive or sensorineural hearing loss reported

imaging: X-rays showing joint contractures and pterygia
genetic: Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern confirmed by family studies
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic multiple pterygia and joint contractures
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant transmission

distinguishingFeatures: Different genetic mutations (e.g., mutations in RAPSN or CHRND genes)
Primarily distal arthrogryposis without multiple pterygia

redFlags: Severe respiratory compromise due to thoracic deformities
Progressive joint contractures leading to significant disability
Feeding difficulties related to cleft palate and facial anomalies
